relationships.subject: allyl isothiocyanate
relationships.evidence_quote: Thus, TRPA1 is implicated in Ca2+-dependent CGRP release that appears to involve high- and low-affinity mechanisms for its activation by AITC.

relationships.subject: A967079
relationships.evidence_quote: An alternative TRPA1 antagonist, A967079, blocked 94 and 88% of CGRP release elicited by 0.05 and 1 mM AITC, respectively (Figure 1C, grey bars).

relationships.subject: BoNT/DA
relationships.evidence_quote: BoNT/DA caused the largest inhibition of AITC-evoked CGRP release, ~75% across the whole range of agonist concentrations tested (Figure 5E).

relationships.subject: BoNT/A
relationships.evidence_quote: Surprisingly, BoNT/A blocked only ~40% of the CGRP release evoked by a broad range of [AITC] (Figure 5E).

relationships.subject: NGF
relationships.evidence_quote: Exposure to NGF for 30 min induced a small but significant (p < 0.0001) increase in CGRP secretion over spontaneous release compared to the amount recorded in the absence of NGF (Figure 6C).

key_findings: AITC evokes CGRP release from trigeminal neurons via a two-site TRPA1 mechanism (EC50 6 and 93 uM).
VAMP-cleaving BoNT/DA inhibited AITC- and capsaicin-evoked CGRP release more than SNAP-25-cleaving BoNT/A; both blocked NGF sensitisation.
